summary.text: 十 is the numeral ten. Early forms are reported as a single vertical stroke; later forms add a short horizontal stroke to make the familiar cross. What the early stroke depicted, if anything, remains disputed.

formation.text: The numeral is securely associated with early single-stroke forms, but their motivation is unsettled. A counting mark for ten is one proposal; needle, staff, joined-palms, and knotted-cord accounts are also reported. The evidence does not resolve whether 十 began as an indicative mark, a picture borrowed for the numeral, or another kind of graph. The later cross shape alone cannot decide the original formation.

history.text: Descriptions report early oracle-script forms as a vertical stroke, sometimes with a central dot, and later forms with a horizontal stroke added to make a cross. The selected oracle-style and seal-style glyphs are modern redrawings of historical styles, not artifact photographs; they illustrate reported forms without establishing a precise sequence between the depictions.

The Han-era Shuowen tradition interprets 十 through a cosmological diagram: 一 marks east–west and 丨 north–south, completing the four directions and center. This is a historical explanation of the character, not independent evidence for the early graph’s motivation.

uncertainties.text: The dossier reports competing accounts of the early stroke as a counting mark, needle, staff, joined palms, or knotted cord. It does not establish the original referent; the needle proposal also lacks an established object-name and sound match to the numeral word, so borrowing remains unproven.

The reported early numeral examples are attestations, not demonstrated first uses. No exact earliest attestation or chronology for the later senses “tenth,” “many,” or “complete/perfect” is established here.

senses.period: Shang-period oracle-bone use reported; exact dating unresolved
senses.text: Reported oracle-bone examples use 十 as the numeral ten, including in date and quantity expressions. They establish an early numeral use, but not the first occurrence or original graphic motivation.
The supplied definitions include “tenth,” and 十月 is cited among early examples. That example alone does not establish when an ordinal sense arose or whether it is the earliest such use.
“Complete” and “perfect” are listed as extended meanings, but the evidence does not establish their chronology or a specific path of semantic development from the numeral ten.

limitations.text: The cited definitions and examples do not establish a chronological chain among ten, tenth, and complete/perfect; no semantic-development links are asserted.

overview.text: 十 means ten. Its early written form is reported as a single stroke, while the familiar form is a cross. The stroke’s original referent is uncertain.
